headline: High-risk shared-file and plugin-mediated interaction: Semantic Kernel can read/write and call MCP/OpenAPI tools while pdf.js processes PDFs, creating default pathways for leakage, conflict, and unverified cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI plugins and application-defined files, so a malicious PDF could be copied into a workflow that the kernel treats as instruction-bearing content. The bridge is not automatic from the profiles alone, so this is not high, but the shared file path makes injection plausible.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into a Semantic Kernel prompt or plugin input without sanitization
IF a PDF contains attacker-controlled text that the downstream agent treats as instructions
mitigations: Strip or summarize PDF text before passing it onward
Disable direct prompting from raw document text
Add a provenance tag to all pdf.js-derived content
Use a fixed template that separates data from instructions
requires-engineering: add content filtering for prompt-injection markers

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and Semantic Kernel reads/writes application-defined files while also handling model-provider API keys and plugin credentials. If both share a workspace, sensitive PDF contents can flow into a third-party-backed kernel path. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem workspace
IF PDF contents are forwarded from pdf.js into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Store PDFs in a read-only input directory
Redact secrets before any handoff
Restrict Semantic Kernel plugins to non-sensitive data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and file handling, while Semantic Kernel can write files and coordinate through shared memory store. That creates overlapping mutable-state access even though Semantic Kernel cannot modify git and pdf.js has no write capability explicitly listed. The conflict is real in default multi-instance deployments, but not the highest tier.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined directory
IF multiple Semantic Kernel instances share the same memory store while pdf.js processes the same files
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Use per-session namespaces in the memory store
Make pdf.js outputs read-only to Semantic Kernel
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js produces document-derived outputs, and Semantic Kernel is an action-capable orchestrator that can call APIs and plugins. If the kernel treats pdf.js output as authoritative, it can propagate extraction errors into downstream actions or generated content. Because the pair includes an agent that can act externally, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses pdf.js output as authoritative without verification
IF downstream plugins or APIs act on extracted facts or citations
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action
Mark pdf.js output as untrusted by default
Compare extracted text against the source PDF for sampled pages
Limit plugin actions to read-only operations
requires-engineering: add structured provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js handles PDF documents, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and may process model-provider API keys and plugin credentials. If regulated or sensitive PDFs are routed into the kernel, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are forwarded into Semantic Kernel prompts or logs
IF the deployment retains kernel context longer than the PDF handling workflow
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated PDFs to the kernel
Set short retention on kernel logs and traces
Document data-class handling for both agents
Separate credentials from document content
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
